title: Open redirect via next parameter to phishing
desc: Login redirect parameter accepted arbitrary URLs. Attacker sends phishing link appearing to be from twitter.com.
steps:
1. Find redirect param: /login?next=https://evil.com
2. Craft phishing email with trusted domain in URL
3. Victim clicks — redirected to attacker site

title: Open redirect via URL parameter — SSRF chain
desc: Open redirect chained with SSRF. Redirect followed server-side, allowing SSRF to internal services.
steps:
1. Find open redirect on target
2. Chain with SSRF: supply redirect URL pointing to internal IP
3. Server follows redirect — reaches internal service

title: Open redirect via OAuth redirect_uri
desc: OAuth redirect_uri parameter accepted arbitrary URLs. Attacker could steal authorization codes.
steps:
1. Start OAuth flow with redirect_uri=https://attacker.com
2. Victim authorizes
3. Code sent to attacker.com — account takeover

title: Open redirect via double slash bypass
desc: Redirect validation blocked http:// but not //. Double slash redirected to attacker-controlled domain.
steps:
1. Test: ?next=//attacker.com
2. Browser interprets as https://attacker.com
3. Redirect follows — victim lands on attacker site

title: Open redirect via @-sign in URL
desc: Redirect validation checked domain but not @-sign. Browser treats everything before @ as credentials.
steps:
1. Craft URL: https://target.com@attacker.com
2. Validation sees target.com — passes
3. Browser redirects to attacker.com
